title: Meet Your Digital Teammate, Hunter: Spotlight on a Sales Agent
summary: Spotlight on Sales: Discover how a digital teammate handles research and outreach so your small business team can focus on closing deals.
body_markdown:
[Try Agentforce](https://www.salesforce.com/sales/ai-sales-agent/?d=bcta)


Meet Hunter. Hunter is a new kind of[digital teammate](https://www.salesforce.com/agentforce/what-is-agentic-ai/agentic-teammates/) for growing businesses — an AI sales agent that works your pipeline around the clock, so your team can spend its time on the conversations that matter. Here’s a look at what Hunter does, how it fits into your day, and why it matters for your next sale.


## What’s an AI sales agent for small business?


An[AI sales agent](https://www.salesforce.com/blog/small-business/selling-with-ai-agents/) isn’t just a chatbot for small business — it’s digital labor that takes on real work in your sales process, autonomously. Instead of assisting a rep one task at a time, these agents live in your business tools, and can research accounts, prioritize prospects, and act on its own, reporting back only when your reps need to step in. AI sales agents help you move sales forward, from prospect nurturing to loyal customer acquisition.


According to our[research](https://www.salesforce.com/news/stories/sales-research-2023/) , Sales reps today spend just 30% of their time actually selling, with the rest eaten up by research, data entry, and cold outreach. A digital teammate for sales flips that ratio back in your favor. Let’s meet Hunter and see what it can do.


## Meet Hunter


[Hunter](https://www.salesforce.com/sales/ai-sales-agent/outbound/) is a prospecting agent inside[Sales Cloud](https://www.salesforce.com/sales/ai-sales-agent/) to cover the full first mile of the deal cycle. Hunter identifies prospects based on buyer intent, researches accounts and contacts, and hands off qualified leads for outreach — no more hours lost to manual research and cold email drafts.


Hunter effectively becomes a sales research and training partner, working from the[customer relationship management (CRM)](https://www.salesforce.com/crm/what-is-crm/) data you already have plus whatever new signals it can find. Let’s find out what Hunter can do.


## A day in the life, with a help agent


So what can Hunter do for your sales team? This is what a real AI sales agent looks like in practice — it’s a coordinated workflow that is trained by your team and executed by your team. Here’s what a day with Hunter actually looks like for growing teams:


- **8:00 AM Prioritize prospect list:** Every morning, Hunter surfaces your best accounts, leads, and contacts to engage, ranked by intent and fit — no more guessing where to start.
- **10:00 AM** **Seamless handoff:** Qualified contacts move straight to the Engagement Agent for automated outreach or into a sales engagement cadence, cutting the gap between “found” and “followed up.”
- **11:00 AM Personalized outreach:** Hunter and Engagement generate emails on the seller’s behalf, handle objections and replies autonomously, and even book meetings.
- **12:00 PM** **Lead nurturing:** Contacts who aren’t ready yet get nurtured through ongoing email conversations instead of falling off the list entirely.


## Why an AI sales agent matters for your pipeline


The business case here isn’t about one task getting faster — it’s about coverage across the whole deal cycle. Hunter holds the target, connects planning, prospecting, and deal management, and keeps your CRM data current without a rep lifting a finger.[Agentforce has generated over 72,000 AI-generated summaries](https://www.salesforce.com/news/stories/how-salesforce-uses-agentforce-sales/) and 43,000-plus personalized emails to support prospecting and outreach.


Take[Raylu](https://www.salesforce.com/customer-stories/raylu-ai/) , a lean revenue team that runs its entire pipeline through Salesforce connected to[Slack](https://www.salesforce.com/slack/) and Claude. With a small team and no dedicated RevOps hire, Raylu built a 2x uplift in pipeline coverage and now tracks richer data on every opportunity — proof that an AI teammate for sales can do the work of a much bigger team.


That kind of coverage matters more than ever. Recent[research](https://www.salesforce.com/ai-research/) shows 88% of small businesses are already engaging with AI, and 74% of those say the investment delivered strong ROI — the shift toward digital teammates isn’t a future bet.


Want to go deeper into how prospecting agents work? Trailhead’s[Agentforce for Sales: Quick Look](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/modules/agentforce-sales-agents-quick-look) module walks through the mechanics in under an hour.

**What is an AI sales agent?**
An AI sales agent is digital labor built into your CRM that can research, prioritize, and act on prospects and leads on its own — not just assist a rep, but actually do the work.


**How is Hunter different from a regular sales tool?**
Most tools require a rep to search and decide. Hunter runs the research and prioritization autonomously, then hands off ready leads for outreach, cutting out the manual legwork entirely.


**Does Hunter replace my sales reps?**
No. Hunter and the Engagement Agent handle research, outreach, and nurturing so your reps can spend their limited time on the conversations that need a human touch — closing deals and building relationships.


**Is Salesforce built for small teams, or just big companies?**
[Sales Cloud](https://www.salesforce.com/sales/cloud/) is built to scale to your ambition, not your headcount — lean teams like[Raylu](https://www.salesforce.com/customer-stories/raylu-ai/) run full pipeline coverage without a dedicated RevOps hire.


**Where can I learn more about setting up an AI sales agent?**
Trailhead’s[Get Ready for Agentforce](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/trails/get-ready-for-agentforce) trail is a solid starting point for understanding how to bring agents like Hunter into your sales process.
